package_info.package_versions: All versions susceptible if not protected
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains source code that leverages Unicode bi-directional (Bidi) control characters to visually obfuscate the true logic of the code, allowing attackers to hide malicious behavior in plain sight. This results in code that appears benign to human reviewers but executes malicious actions, undermining code review and supply chain security.

execution_context.file_location: Any source file (e.g., main.py, index.js, etc.)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code uses Unicode Bidi control characters to visually reorder tokens, causing the logic to execute grantAccess() for guest users while appearing to only grant access to admins.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of Unicode Bidi control characters in source code is highly unusual and can be used to visually obfuscate the true logic of the code, making it difficult for human reviewers to detect malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal code should not contain invisible Unicode control characters that alter the logical flow of execution. The actual behavior (granting access to guests) is hidden from reviewers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Bidi characters are legitimate in internationalized text content, but not in code logic or control flow.
key_indicators: Presence of Unicode Bidi control characters (e.g., U+202E, U+202A, U+202B, U+202C, U+2066, U+2067, U+2068, U+2069)
Mismatch between displayed code and actual execution logic
Obfuscated or misleading comments and control flow

attack_chain.action: Attacker injects Unicode Bidi control characters into source code to visually reorder code tokens.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious logic is hidden from code reviewers.

attack_chain.action: Code is reviewed and appears benign due to visual obfuscation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is merged and deployed.

attack_chain.action: At runtime, the actual logic executes as intended by the attacker (e.g., privilege escalation, data exfiltration).
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromise of application security or data.

behavioral_signatures: Presence of Unicode Bidi control characters in source code files
Mismatch between displayed code logic and actual execution logic
Unexpected privilege escalation or logic inversion at runtime
file_indicators: Source files containing Unicode Bidi control characters (U+202E, U+202A, U+202B, U+202C, U+2066, U+2067, U+2068, U+2069)
Comments or strings that appear to close code blocks or invert logic
network_indicators: Not directly network-related, but may be combined with exfiltration logic hidden via Bidi characters
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan all source code files for the presence of Unicode Bidi control characters. Flag any files containing these characters for manual review. Use automated tools to compare the logical execution order of code with its visual representation. Integrate Unicode character detection into CI/CD pipelines to block code containing suspicious Bidi characters before deployment.
